title: Reduction of the cokernel of a strict cone-inclusion lift
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, $E$ an $R/I$-complex, and $K,A$ complexes of $R$-modules. Let $\delta:E\to (R/I)\otimes_R K$ be any chain map, and $e:(R/I)\otimes_R A\cong\operatorname{Cone}(\delta)$ an isomorphism. Suppose $f:K\to A$ reduces, after e, to the cone inclusion. Then the reduction of the actual cokernel complex of f is isomorphic to $E[1]$. The reduction of the actual cokernel sequence of f is split in every degree. Neither injectivity of f nor acyclicity of any complex is assumed.

proof.text: The rotated cone short complex is degreewise split by mappingCone.triangleRotateShortComplexSplitting. It is short exact, so its second arrow is a cokernel of its first arrow.

Extension of scalars preserves cokernels of complexes. Compose PreservesCokernel.iso with cokernel.mapIso from the strict-square equality and the unique isomorphism to the rotated cone short complex cokernel. This gives the reduced cokernel isomorphism to E[1].

The cokernel comparison, the commuting-square induced cokernel map, and the cokernel universal-property isomorphism commute with projections. Build a ShortComplex.isoMk from the reduced cokernel sequence to the rotated cone sequence. Evaluate and transport its splitting to obtain the asserted degreewise splittings.
